bull.b: Rapid revenue expansion and a deeply contracted backlog provide substantial visibility into future demand and utilization. This supports continued scaling of the infrastructure platform, strengthens customer relevance in AI computing, and can sustain growth over the next several quarters.

The high adjusted EBITDA margin indicates that GPU infrastructure can generate attractive operating economics once deployed and utilized. Continued scale may improve absorption of fixed platform costs, supporting operating leverage and helping fund expansion despite substantial capital requirements.

Growth in managed inference and demonstrated technical performance broaden the company beyond raw GPU access toward higher-value AI services. Greater platform functionality can deepen customer integration, improve differentiation, and support recurring demand as training and inference workloads expand.

bear.b: Very high leverage reduces financial flexibility and leaves the company more exposed to refinancing conditions, interest costs, and execution setbacks. The debt-funded capital structure may constrain future investment choices and increases the financial burden of maintaining rapid capacity growth.

Operating cash generation currently does not cover the capital required to expand the GPU infrastructure base. Persistently negative free cash flow means growth depends on substantial external financing or continued capital access, increasing funding requirements and sensitivity to deployment execution.

Growing interest expense is absorbing more of the company’s operating earnings while GAAP losses remain substantial. This weakens earnings conversion, limits internally funded growth, and makes profitability increasingly dependent on higher utilization, margin improvement, and successful capacity deployment.
